thread:
sophia: Heads up — saw a weird split handoff in a private VPC canary. Traffic jumped 1% -> 50% because a control-plane delta applied out of order.
Aj: Ugh. Which sync path was that on? push or poll for that customer?
kevin: @sophia can you paste the rollout config and any logs you have? also, did routing have a fallback rule enabled?
sophia: It was a poll-based private instance (airgapped-ish). Control plane bundles delayed ~12m. Routing had fallback but the split fraction applied atomically when bundle landed. Config snippet: ```
rollout:
  mode: canary
  splits: [0.01, 0.5]
  sync: poll
  sync_interval: 30s
  grace_window: 5m
```
ingrid: We currently treat grace_window for route table changes only, not for split fraction deltas — that might be the root cause.
Aj: Right. For poll-based clients we bundle a sequence number and apply the bundle atomically. If bundles arrive out-of-order (or we rehydrate from disk) you can see a flip.
sam: deploy-bot showed repeated 429s and timeouts to the private-controlplane during the gap. Logs: ```
[2026-03-19T14:02:11Z] controlplane: 429 throttle
[2026-03-19T14:08:20Z] sync: bundle v12 received
[2026-03-19T14:08:21Z] client: apply bundle v12 -> splits set to 50%
```
kevin: Two high-level options: 1) require strict monotonic seq checks on client and reject out-of-order bundles, 2) allow client-side gradual application (max-increment) to avoid big jumps.
ingrid: Monotonic seq + reject is safest for correctness, but UX is rough: if a client misses a bundle it stalls until operator pushes again. For airgapped customers that can be annoying.
sophia: Proposal: introduce a client flag `staged_apply` with a `max_increment` default. If `staged_apply=true` and seq is newer, client applies in steps with short local backoff to smooth changes. Example: ```
client_rollout_behavior:
  staged_apply: true
  max_increment_pct: 10
  staged_interval: 15s
```
Aj: Also we should expose last-seen seq and pending bundle age in the Console so operators can see staleness per private deployment. Ops have been asking for per-deployment lag metrics.
sam: I'll add two telemetry metrics: `controlplane_lag_seconds` and `last_applied_seq` (gauge). Dashboard tile idea: staleness + a small sparkline.
kevin: I'll draft an RFC to bump the bundle schema to include `seq` and an optional `delta_chain` field so clients can replay missing deltas if available. Link (draft): https://redwood.internal/rfc/270 
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated on cluster-private-47 after split flip detected :rotating_light:
sophia: Thanks — I'll correlate server logs with the rollback and propose conservative defaults for private: `poll_interval=60s`, `max_increment_pct=10`, `require_seq=true`.
ingrid: I'll add a minimal Console indicator that shows `bundle_age` and a yellow caution if > 2m.
Aj: Great. @kevin can you own the RFC? I can prototype server-side enforcement for `require_seq` and a `bundle_watermark` to avoid accidental replays.
kevin: On it. I'll create the RFC, tag eng-platform + eng-runtime, and include a migration plan for private customers.
ops-bot: ops-bot: Created ticket #PLT-4821 to track console telemetry + dashboard work.
sophia: Cool. Thanks everyone — prioritizing this for next sprint to avoid noisy rollouts in private/VPC environments.
